name: sol_defi_oracle_5
description: TWAP oracle period set too short, enabling price manipulation via short-window time-weighted average price
question: The source file in `source` computes or configures a TWAP oracle price using a time period/window that is too short (e.g., a few seconds, a single block, or zero) or that can be set/changed to such a short value without any minimum-bound validation, so an attacker can manipulate the price within that window (e.g., via flash loan or same-block trades) and have it accepted as the TWAP; this excludes code that hardcodes or validates a sufficiently long TWAP period (e.g., tens of minutes or more) or that uses the price for non-critical, manipulation-resistant purposes.
criteria: Calls a TWAP consult/observe function with a hardcoded secondsAgo/period of 1 second or a single block
Passes a period value of 0 to the oracle, causing it to effectively return the current spot price instead of a time-weighted average
Stores twapPeriod as an owner-settable state variable used directly in oracle calls with no minimum value enforced in the setter
Computes TWAP as (currentTick - tickAtLastUpdate) over an interval that can be arbitrarily small because lastUpdate is not rate-limited
